sections.title: What Kind of Doctor Should You See After a Car Accident?

paras.t: Not everyone needs the ER after a wreck, but everyone should get checked. Here's who does what, and in what order.

sections.name: Doctors Section
sections.title: The doctors who treat car accident injuries

cards.title: Emergency room or urgent care
cards.text: Rules out the serious stuff: fractures, internal injuries, concussion. They stabilize you. They usually don't treat the neck and back pain that shows up days later.

cards.title: Your family doctor
cards.text: Can check you over, document your injuries, and refer you on. Some family doctors aren't set up to bill auto insurance, which can slow things down.

cards.title: Chiropractor
cards.text: Treats the neck and back injuries that crashes cause most: whiplash, back pain, pinched nerves, disc problems. A crash-focused exam and imaging on day one also documents the injury from the start.

cards.title: MRI and specialists
cards.text: If an injury needs a closer look or a different kind of care, a chiropractor refers you on: for an MRI, to an orthopedic surgeon for fractures or torn ligaments, to a neurologist for concussion or nerve problems, or to pain management.

sections.name: How We Fit In Section
sections.title: What happens when you come here

paras.t: Dr. Morgan's crash exam focuses on how the crash actually happened: which direction, whether you were braced, where you felt it first. Digital X-rays happen on site, and he shows you what he sees the same visit.

Because disc injuries are more likely after a crash, he refers most car accident patients for an MRI. If anything points to a specialist, he'll send you to one. Crash injuries are usually acute, so care starts out frequent to stabilize things, and plans typically run 24 to 48 visits.

faqs.q: Should I see my family doctor or a chiropractor first?
faqs.a: If anything on the ER list applies, go there first. Otherwise, either is a reasonable first stop. A chiropractor who works with car accident patients can examine, image, and document your injuries the same day, and refer you on if needed.
Often, yes. Disc injuries are more likely after a crash, so Dr. Morgan refers most car accident patients for an MRI.
In most cases, no. PIP, a letter of protection, or a third-party claim usually covers it.

faqs.q: How soon can I be seen?
faqs.a: Often the same day. Call and tell us you were in an accident.
